skill.name: sqlite-ops
skill.description: Provides SQLite patterns for Python projects, including schema design, local state, caching, migrations, WAL mode, and async access with aiosqlite.
skill.summary: Use proven SQLite patterns for Python state, cache, migration, and async workflows.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences, placeholder SQLite filenames, SQL identifiers, and sample private IP data. No prompt injection attempt or malicious network intent was found. One semantic issue remains: examples interpolate field names into SQL without validation.

remediation.suggestion: Whitelist allowed column names and JSON fields before building SQL. Keep user supplied values in parameter bindings only.

remediation.issue: SQLite dump and restore examples can expose local data
remediation.suggestion: Add a note to run CLI examples only on intended databases and to protect exported dumps and backups.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Dynamic SQL Field Interpolation
semantic_findings.description: Example code interpolates caller supplied field names into SQL text before binding values. If copied with untrusted fields, this can allow SQL injection through identifiers or JSON paths.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both examples use f-strings to insert field names into SQL while only values are parameterized. The risk depends on caller control, so confidence is high but not absolute.

content.value_statement: SQLite projects need safe patterns for schemas, migrations, caching, and async access. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reusable Python SQLite guidance.
actual_capabilities: Shows Python sqlite3 connection setup with row factories, WAL mode, and foreign key enforcement.
Provides schema patterns for state storage, caches, events, queues, sessions, and full text search.
Explains migration patterns with version tracking, named migrations, rollbacks, and table recreation.
Covers aiosqlite CRUD, batching, pooling, streaming, concurrent queries, and error handling.
Includes SQLite CLI examples for schema checks, dumps, restores, and schema comparison.
limitations: It provides examples and patterns, not a complete database framework.
It focuses on SQLite for Python projects and does not cover other database engines.
Some examples require aiosqlite, which is not part of the Python standard library.
Applications must adapt schema names, indexes, and transaction boundaries to their workload.

use_cases.title: Plan Schema Migrations

use_cases.title: Improve Async Database Access
use_cases.description: Use aiosqlite patterns for CRUD, batching, streaming, and concurrent query workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic SQLite Store
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for local state or cache data.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a simple SQLite table for local application state. Include indexes, timestamps, and basic access patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Add Async CRUD Patterns
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate aiosqlite access for an existing table.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me an aiosqlite CRUD pattern for my table. Use parameter binding, transactions, and clear error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Design Versioned Migrations
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced schema evolution for a growing project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SQLite migration approach for my Python project. Include version tracking, named migrations, rollback limits, and verification steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review a SQLite Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of performance and safety tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my SQLite design for concurrency, indexes, WAL mode, migrations, and data safety. Highlight risks and practical improvements.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for a cache table with expiry cleanup.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests a cache schema with expiry timestamps, an expiry index, and cleanup guidance for stale rows.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks for async reads and writes.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines an aiosqlite connection pattern, parameterized statements, transaction commits, and common error handling cases.

output_examples.input: A team asks how to evolve a local database schema.
output_examples.output: The skill describes version tracking, migration ordering, rollback caveats, table recreation steps, and CLI verification checks.

best_practices: Use parameter binding for all user supplied values and validate any dynamic identifiers.
Enable WAL mode and foreign keys when the application needs concurrency and referential integrity.
Test migrations on database copies before applying them to important local data.
anti_patterns: Do not concatenate untrusted strings into SQL statements or JSON paths.
Do not run dump, restore, or migration commands against production data without backups.
Do not use SQLite as a replacement for a multi writer server database under heavy write load.

faq.question: Does this skill install a SQLite library?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Python sqlite3 is built in, and async examples require aiosqlite.

faq.question: Can it design a schema for local application state?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes patterns for state, cache, event, queue, session, and search tables.

faq.question: Does it support async Python applications?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers aiosqlite connections, CRUD operations, batching, pooling, streaming, and concurrent queries.

faq.question: Can it help with migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains version tables, named migrations, rollback handling, table recreation, and CLI checks.

faq.question: Is every example production ready?
faq.answer: No. Treat examples as starting points and adapt validation, backups, indexes, and transactions for your application.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
